title: throughput-quality-knee-analysis-jul2025
body:
Purpose:
This is a lab-style report and working notebook for a focused set of onboarding experiments that try to locate the "knee" (inflection point) in the latency vs cost vs quality tradeoff for candidate models during onboarding. The goal is to output a small set of operational knobs (batch size, prefix caching policy, max_tokens cap) and an automated rule for recommending defaults for Hosted and Dedicated tiers.

Context and motivation:
- Prior sweeps looked at broad latency/cost matrices but we lack a repeatable heuristic to pick the sweet spot where marginal cost increases stop justifying quality gains.
- For customers we want a single recommended config per model+prompt-set that meets a quality SLA (task-specific) while minimizing per-token cost and keeping p95 latency under tier targets.

High-level approach:
1) Use a representative promptset split into short/medium/long buckets (see PromptSet description below). Evaluate each bucket independently to see different knee locations.
2) Sweep batch sizes B = [1,2,4,8,16] and max_tokens M = [64,128,256,512]. Two cache modes: prefix-cache=off, prefix-cache=on (warm kv-cache).
3) For each (B,M,cache) measure: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, cost_per_response (USD normalized), and quality metric Q (task-specific; exact-match for QA, BLEU for summarization; normalized 0-1).
4) Compute incremental cost per unit quality (delta_cost / delta_Q) across increasing B and M; identify knee by looking for the first point where delta_cost/delta_Q > threshold T (empirically 0.03 USD per 0.01 quality point for our workloads).

PromptSet composition (representative sample):
- short (1-2 sentence prompts): 600 samples (30%)
- medium (3-6 sentence prompts): 900 samples (45%)
- long (6-20 sentence prompts): 500 samples (25%)
Notes: prompts are mixed across tasks: extractive QA (40%), summarization (35%), conversational completion (25%).

Experiment run details:
- Model: open-llm-v2-medium-16k (quantized FP16 runtime backend)
- Hardware: Dedicated A100x4 (shared test rig)
- Runtime: r-runtime-v1.4.2-debug build with live KV cache instrumentation
- Measurement tooling: internal loadgen + trace-exporter -> parquet.
- Cost normalization: use our internal cost model (gpu-minutes -> USD) and token accounting per response.

Observations and analysis (quick):
- Caching consistently lowers p95 by ~10-15% at low B; benefit shrinks as B increases because batching amortizes KV costs.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) scales sublinearly after B=8; p95 balloons for long prompts once B >= 8 due to memory and KV pressure.
- Quality Q shows diminishing returns for larger M beyond 256 for short/medium prompts; long prompts get small quality uplift up to 256 but plateau thereafter.
- Cost/resp decreases with higher B but quality may drop slightly due to quantization / tail truncation interactions for tiny prompts when B is large.

Knee detection heuristic (working):
- For each prompt bucket, plot cost vs quality and compute the discrete marginal ratio r_i = (cost_i - cost_{i-1}) / (Q_i - Q_{i-1}).
- Flag the knee at the first i where r_i > 3x median(r) across sweep OR r_i > absolute threshold 0.03 USD/0.01Q (tunable).
- For short prompts in this run the heuristic picks B=2, M=64, cache=on (keeps p95 < 125ms, Q=0.83, cost small).
- For medium prompts picks B=4, M=128, cache=on (balanced throughput and p95 ~330ms).
- For long prompts picks B=2, M=256, cache=on (avoids p95 blowups while preserving Q).

Operational recommendations (draft):
- Default onboarding recommendation: run automated sweep on the first 2k representative prompts (bucketed by length). Use the knee heuristic above with default thresholds; produce a "recommended config" plus two fallbacks: "low-latency" (force B<=2, cache=on, lower M) and "high-throughput" (allow B up to 8 with auto-fallback if p95 > target).
- Machine-tier guidance: use stricter p95 guardrails for Hosted (p95 target: 250ms short, 600ms medium, 1500ms long) and looser for Dedicated (customer-defined).
- Add a regression check in onboarding pipeline: when a new model version is onboarded run the sweep and compare recommended config Q against reference baseline; fail onboarding if Q delta < -0.02 and p95 worsened > 20%.

Open questions and next steps:
- Need to formalize cost model for GPUs with mixed occupancy and power scaling; current USD/resp is a simplification.
- Investigate why tiny prompt Q drops with very large batches — hypothesis: microtiming changes in quantized kernels + increased sampling concurrency. Create a microbench.
- Add synthetic jitter to loadgen to emulate real traffic patterns for p95 sensitivity.
- Create a visualization page (Confluence + small web UI) that displays cost-quality frontier and knee point per model+promptset.

Quick action items (owners):
- (Avery) wire knee detection into onboarding job script, add unit tests for ratio calculations. (due 2025-07-17)
- (Samir) build microbench for sampling concurrency effects on small prompts. (due 2025-07-24)

- (Jonas) tune loadgen to add traffic jitter and run long-tail p95 tests. (due 2025-07-22)

Appendix: quick reproducibility notes
- Command used (example): 
  ./onboard-sweep --model open-llm-v2-medium-16k --prompts promptset_v20250703.json --batches 1,2,4,8,16 --max-tokens 64,128,256,512 --cache-modes on,off --out results/throughput-quality-20250703.parquet
- Data artifacts location: gs://redwood-onboard/experiments/2025-07-03/throughput-quality-*/
- Expected parity: results should be within ±10% tokens/sec and ±0.02 Q for comparable hardware.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- This doc intentionally mixes raw numbers and heuristics — convert to a polished runbook if team agrees on thresholds.
- Might extract long-prompt-heavy samples into a separate eval to avoid noisy mixing.
